Article Title: PM Modi hails youth for taking India to arenas once beyond reach
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi

NEW DELHI: From PV Sindhu 's racquet in Tokyo to a privately built rocket lifting off from Sriharikota, PM Narendra Modi Sunday used Mann Ki Baat to say young Indians were taking the country into arenas once considered beyond reach.In his monthly radio address, Modi singled out Sindhu's Japan Open triumph, the launch of Vikram-1, and India's performance at international science Olympiads as signs of a confident generation succeeding in sports, science and technology."Our youth have achieved remarkable feats in sports recently. PV Sindhu has become the first Indian to win the Japan Open title in badminton; the entire nation is proud of this achievement of hers," Modi said.Turning to space, he said Vikram-1, India's first privately developed orbital rocket, showed what young innovators could achieve when new doors were opened. Built by Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace, it placed six payloads in low-Earth orbit on July 18. "Keeping the interests of the youth in mind, we opened up the space sector to private enterprise, and today, the world is witnessing the results."He praised school students for winning 12 gold and seven silver medals across physics, chemistry, biology and mathematics Olympiads.Meanwhile, he lauded the youth as the energy behind the resolve of a developed India and said they will also be its biggest beneficiary as he held a virtual interaction with young participants of "Viksit Vibrant Village" programme. "When the youth directly connect with the country's challenges and their solutions, then the future will certainly be bright," he said.Speaking to youngsters who had visited border villages as part of a govt initiative, he said, "The more India's youth understand its border villages, the more easily they will know the country and connect with all its corners."
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi sunday used mann ki baat to say young indians were taking the country into arenas once considered beyond reach. He singled out sindhu's japan open triumph, the launch of vikram-1, and india's performance at international science olympiads.

Article Title: 'Wapis nahi aane dega': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's form triggers fresh debate over Sanju Samson's India return
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Sanju Samson

Selection battle ahead

NEW DELHI: Former India cricketer Irfan Pathan suggests that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s impressive performances could make it difficult for anyone, including Sanju Samson , to reclaim his place in India’s T20I side.The young batter continued his fine form with a composed 81-run innings in the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe on July 26, showing both maturity and power on a challenging Harare pitch.He played some eye-catching shots, including a straight drive off a yorker from Brad Evans and a massive 102-metre six against Sikandar Raza.Praising the youngster, Pathan wrote, “Jiski vhi jagah lega ye bachha use wapis nahi aane dega…How Special this Vaibhav Suryavanshi is??" (Whoever's place this kid takes, he won't let them come back. How special is this Vaibhav Suryavanshi?)His comments have added to the debate over whether Sooryavanshi has moved ahead of Samson in India’s T20 plans.Samson started as India’s first-choice opener during the Ireland T20Is but managed only low scores, leading to Sooryavanshi getting opportunities in the England series.Although the youngster couldn’t produce big knocks consistently in that series and Samson returned for the fifth T20I, neither change helped India avoid a whitewash.Samson was then left out of the Zimbabwe T20I series, while Sooryavanshi grabbed his chance with another impressive innings. With India’s next T20 assignment set to be the Asian Games, the competition for the opening spot between Samson and Sooryavanshi is expected to remain a major talking point.At the same time, Abhishek Sharma ’s place at the top has also come under scrutiny after a poor run of scores. The opener has managed just 2, 8, 1, 3, 16 and 10 in his last six T20I innings, raising fresh questions over India’s preferred opening combination.

Article Title: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation
Article Text:
The name 'Anahat' came from Guru Nanak's prayer

Aad aneel anaad anaahat jug jug ayko vays

Anahat stays true to its meaning

READ ALSO:

NEW DELHI:. This exact line appears once at the close of four consecutive stanzas, Pauris 28, 29, 30, and 31, of Japji Sahib, composed by Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, in the opening composition of the Guru Granth Sahib.Translated, it reads roughly as: The One is primal, stainless, without beginning, self-existent (unstruck), and the same throughout all ages.Japji Sahib opens the Guru Granth Sahib, Sikhism's central scripture, and it's the prayer devout Sikhs recite every morning as part of their daily practice. Tucked inside that refrain is the word anaahat, which means unstruck, unbeaten, a sound that exists without ever being produced by collision. It is also, as it happens, the name of one of Indian sport's most exciting young athletes, Anahat Singh."My husband came up with it," Anahat's mother, Tani Vadera Singh, had earlier told TimesofIndia.com . "He was reading the Sikh prayer, Japji Sahib. And in the last line, there is, he knows it, the name Anahat."On March 13, 2008, Gursharan Singh was reading the prayer in the hospital room the day his daughter was born. Something about the word stopped him."He said, you know, this sounds really nice," Tani recalled."I would like to name her that. So that is how (Anahat was named)."There was no grand plan behind it, and there wasn't one behind her sporting career either, at least not at first.The Singh-Vadera household was simply a sporting one. Tani played hockey for Delhi at the sub-junior and junior levels; Gursharan played hockey at St. Stephen's College and had hoped to play for India before academics took over. Uncle Deepak Vadera was once one of India's finest table tennis players. Anahat's elder sister, Amira, played tennis before switching to squash, and Anahat herself started on badminton at six, following the family's simple house rule that sport mattered as much as school."We always feel that sport is as important as studies," Tani admitted.Anahat trailed her sister into squash next, and the family openly admits they had no idea what they were building. "We didn't obviously imagine all this happening," Tani added. "We were just playing for fun."Father Gursharan, who'd never played the sport himself, taught himself squash so he could help train her, working alongside her coaches. It stayed lighthearted for years, Anahat wanting, as a five-year-old, to be an Olympic champion, though she was picturing badminton at the time, not the sport she'd eventually take to a world stage.The turn toward seriousness came once she made the Commonwealth Games squad at 13, a milestone her mother pinpoints as the moment "fun" started sharing space with real expectation.That balance of joy and intensity has produced a résumé most players twice her age would envy.Anahat debuted for India at 14 at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, won Asian Games medals at 16, and climbed inside the world's top 20 as she transitioned onto the senior circuit.On Saturday, the 18-year-old added the achievement that may end up defining her junior career, having become the first Indian ever to win the World Junior Squash Championship, beating Egypt's Ruqayya Salem 3-0 in the final in Niagara-on-the-Lake, Canada, without dropping a single game across the whole tournament.She'd beaten two other Egyptian players en route, a country that had held this exact title for sixteen consecutive years running. The last non-Egyptian to win it at all was American Amanda Sobhy, back in 2010.It's a fitting full circle. A name lifted from Guru Nanak's prayer has travelled from the rhythm of a morning recitation to the biggest stage in junior squash. Anahat Singh gave it a new association of her own by living up to the poise and permanence it has come to represent.
Article Summary: Anahat singh is the first indian ever to win the world junior squash championship. She beat egypt's ruqayya salem 3-0 in the final in niagara-on-the-lake, canada. The 18-year-old's name comes from a line in guru nanak's prayer, japji sahib. Anahat's mother tani vadera singh says her husband came up with the name.

Article Title: Commonwealth Games 2026 medal table: Where India stands after Mirabai Chanu's golden hat-trick in Glasgow
Article Text:
INDIA AT COMMONWEALTH GAMES 2026

Mirabai Chanu creates history with third straight Commonwealth Games gold

Rishikanta Singh claims silver after equalling Games record



Raja Muthupandi completes India's weightlifting medal haul





Boxers continue strong campaign







Relay team reaches swimming final





Mixed fortunes in bowls and gymnastics





India's Day 4 results





Weightlifting

Mirabai Chanu won gold in the women's 48kg event.

Rishikanta Singh won silver in the men's 60kg event.

Raja Muthupandi won silver in the men's 65kg event.

Boxing

Jadumani Singh defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman 5-0 (men's 55kg Round of 16).

Preeti Pawar defeated Malawi's Deborah Mtenje by RSC (women's 54kg Round of 16).

Aditya Pratap Yadav lost 3-2 to Uganda's Nuhu Batte (men's 65kg Round of 16).

The same quartet later finished sixth in the final.

Women's pairs: India lost to Namibia in a tiebreak and later lost to England, exiting the competition.

Men's singles: Putul Sonowal lost to Malta's Shaun James Parnis.

Artistic Gymnastics

3x3 Wheelchair Basketball

India lost 21-4 to Scotland in Women's Pool B.

CWG 2026 Glasgow Medal Standings (So Far)



CWG 2026 Medal Table standings

India enjoyed its most successful day so far at the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Sunday, collecting one gold and two silver medals to take its overall tally to four medals, while boxers continued their impressive run and the men's swimming relay team reached another Commonwealth final.Olympic silver medallist Mirabai Chanu headlined India's Day 4 performances by winning her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal, while Rishikanta Singh and Raja Muthupandi added silver medals in weightlifting. Elsewhere, Jadumani Singh booked his place in the boxing quarter-finals with a commanding victory over Pakistan's Sumama Rehman, Preeti Pawar advanced with a stoppage win, and the men's 4x200m freestyle relay team qualified for and competed in the final.Saikhom Mirabai Chanu once again underlined her status as one of India's greatest weightlifters by winning the women's 48kg gold medal.The Tokyo Olympic silver medallist overcame an unsuccessful opening attempt before producing another dominant performance, finishing with a combined lift of 190kg. She set a new Commonwealth Games record of 85kg in the snatch before lifting 105kg in the clean and jerk to comfortably secure the title.The victory completed a remarkable hat-trick of Commonwealth Games gold medals after her triumphs in Gold Coast in 2018 and Birmingham in 2022. It also took her overall Commonwealth Games medal tally to four.Rishikanta Singh Chanambam delivered an outstanding performance to secure silver in the men's 60kg event.The 28-year-old lifter from Manipur successfully cleared 116kg, 119kg and 121kg in the snatch, with his best effort equalling the Commonwealth Games record.He then managed 143kg in the clean and jerk but narrowly missed attempts at 148kg and 151kg, finishing with a total lift of 264kg.Malaysia's Muhammad Anik bin Kasdan won gold with a Games-record total of 273kg, while Kenya's Joshua Amunga Buoya claimed bronze after lifting 260kg.Raja Muthupandi ensured India finished the day with three weightlifting medals by taking silver in the men's 65kg category.The Tamil Nadu lifter recorded 126kg in the snatch before adding 160kg in the clean and jerk to finish with a combined total of 286kg.Malaysia's Muhamad Aznil Bin Bidin captured gold after setting a Commonwealth Games record total of 299kg, while Papua New Guinea's Morea Baru secured bronze with 282kg.The silver capped a remarkable comeback for Muthupandi, who returned to the Commonwealth Games podium eight years after finishing sixth on his debut at Gold Coast in 2018 following an injury-disrupted spell that also saw him miss Birmingham 2022.India enjoyed another productive day inside the boxing ring.Jadumani Singh Mandengbam defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the men's 55kg Round of 16 to book his place in the quarter-finals.After a closely contested opening round, the Manipur boxer gradually took control of the contest, scoring a knockdown in the second round before sealing victory on all five judges' scorecards. He will next face England's Ellis Trowbridge for a place in the medal rounds.In the women's 54kg Round of 16, Preeti Pawar produced a dominant display to defeat Malawi's Deborah Mtenje by referee stops contest (RSC), advancing comfortably to the quarter-finals.India also suffered one boxing setback as Aditya Pratap Yadav narrowly lost to Uganda's Nuhu Batte in the men's 65kg Round of 16 by a 3-2 split decision.India's men's 4x200m freestyle relay quartet of Srihari Nataraj, Aryan Nehra, Aneesh Gowda and Dhakshan Shashikumar successfully qualified for the final after finishing third in Heat 2.The Indian team clocked 7:39.48 to finish behind Australia and England while holding off Jersey to secure progression. They advanced as the sixth-fastest team overall from the combined heats.Later in the evening, the same quartet returned for the medal race and finished sixth in the Commonwealth Games final.India endured a difficult day in lawn bowls.Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh first lost 3-0 to Namibia in a women's pairs sectional play tiebreak before suffering another defeat against England, ending their campaign in the event.In the men's singles, Putul Sonowal lost his sectional play match against Malta's Shaun James Parnis.Artistic gymnast Tapan Mohanty finished 15th in the men's all-around final.India's women's 3x3 wheelchair basketball team also suffered defeat, losing 21-4 to Scotland in Pool B.India concluded Day 4 with four medals overall at the Games; one gold, two silvers and one bronze, with the boxing contingent continuing to build momentum heading into the quarter-final stage.
Article Summary: India enjoyed its most successful day so far at the 2026 commonwealth games on sunday, collecting one gold and two silver medals. Olympic silver medallist mirabai chanu won her third consecutive commonwealth games gold medal. Rishikanta singh and raja muthupandi added silver medals in weightlifting.

Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, creates world record at just 15
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (ANI Photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view What impressed you the most about Sooryavanshi's performance in Zimbabwe? His ability to adapt to different pitches. His consistency across matches. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi added another milestone to his remarkable start in international cricket after becoming the youngest player to win a Player of the Series award in men's international cricket.The 15-year-old achieved the feat after starring in India's 3-0 T20I series sweep over Zimbabwe in Harare. Sooryavanshi finished as the leading run-scorer of the series with 151 runs in three innings and capped off the campaign with a match-winning 81 off 49 balls in the final T20I.The left-handed opener showed impressive adaptability throughout the series. After announcing himself with a blistering 50 off just 18 balls in the opening match, Sooryavanshi produced a more measured innings in the decider on a sluggish pitch. His knock of 81, laced with eight fours and four sixes, powered India to 192/5 before the visitors completed a 35-run victory.His consistency across the three matches earned him the Player of the Series award, making him the youngest recipient of the honour in men's international cricket.Speaking after receiving the award, Sooryavanshi credited his preparation for the successful series."I try to replicate what I do in training," he said. "I had good preparation time after the England tour and I am glad to score these runs for the team, and contribute to the series win.It was my dream to do it for India."The award marked a significant turnaround for the teenager, who had endured a difficult maiden international series in England earlier this month. After replacing Sachin Tendulkar as India's youngest men's international cricketer, Sooryavanshi managed scores of 14, 13 and 15 in the T20I series against England before being left out of the final game, which India also lost to concede the series 4-0.However, the selectors persisted with the young batter for the Zimbabwe tour, backing him to rediscover the form that had made him one of India's brightest prospects. Their faith was rewarded as Sooryavanshi dominated at the Harare Sports Club, a venue where he had already made headlines earlier this year with a stunning 175 off 80 balls against England in the Under-19 World Cup final.His latest achievement further underlined his rapid rise, with the teenager not only playing a decisive role in India's series victory but also entering the record books as the youngest-ever Player of the Series winner in men's international cricket.
Article Summary: Vaibhav sooryavanshi becomes youngest player of the series winner in men's international cricket. The 15-year-old starred in india's 3-0 t20i series sweep over zimbabwe in harare. He finished as the leading run-scorer of the series with 151 runs in three innings and capped off the campaign with a match-winning 81 off 49 balls.

Article Title: 'Dedicate my win to Kargil heroes': Indian boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam after beating Pakistan's Sumama Rehman at CWG 2026
Article Text:
India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)

Indian boxer Jadumani Singh Mandengbam moved into the men's 55kg quarterfinals at the Commonwealth Games 2026 after defeating Pakistan's Sumama Rehman by a unanimous 5-0 decision on Sunday.The convincing victory came on Kargil Vijay Diwas , making the win even more special for the 22-year-old, who dedicated it to India's Kargil War heroes.After the bout, Jadumani said, "I dedicate my win to the Kargil heroes. I felt great winning against Pakistan. I will perform even better in the quaterfinals and secure a Gold for India."His victory coincided with the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas, when India honoured the soldiers who sacrificed their lives during the 1999 Kargil War. Jadumani stayed in control throughout the contest against Rehman, earning all five judges' votes to seal a comfortable win.The Manipuri boxer had already impressed in the opening round with another 5-0 win over Scotland's Aaron Cullen. His latest victory takes him into the last eight, where he will fight on Tuesday for a place in the semifinals.A win in the quarterfinal will also guarantee him at least a bronze medal, as both losing semifinalists in Commonwealth Games boxing receive bronze.Jadumani, who won silver in the 50kg category at last year's World Boxing Cup Finals before moving up to the 55kg division, has looked in excellent form with back-to-back unanimous victories.India also enjoyed success in other events on Sunday, with Mirabai Chanu winning her third straight Commonwealth Games gold in weightlifting, while Chanambam Rishikanta Singh and Raja Muthupandi claimed silver medals, adding to the country's strong medal haul in Glasgow.
Article Summary: Jadumani singh mandengbam beats sumama rehman by unanimous 5-0 decision. The 22-year-old will now face scotland's aaron cullen in the quarterfinals. Mirabai chanu won her third straight commonwealth games gold in weightlifting.

Stefon Diggs remains a free agent with training camps already underway, but the wait may finally be ending. After a legal cloud that lingered over his market cleared last month, fresh reporting from ESPN's Jeremy Fowler now points to one team pulling ahead of the pack: the Washington Commanders. Here's everything currently known about where the four-time Pro Bowler could land.Washington has emerged as the clear favorite. According to Fowler, the Commanders still need a true complement to Terry McLaurin, and word around the league is that a receiver addition "should shake out" for Diggs sooner rather than later. Diggs also has local ties as a Maryland native, adding a hometown angle to the fit.Washington had been floated as a landing spot for Brandon Aiyuk earlier in the offseason, but his recent combative social media activity has reportedly given the front office cold feet, clearing a path for Diggs instead.The Baltimore Ravens have also been mentioned as a fallback suitor, given questions about their receiver depth behind Zay Flowers, though Washington remains the far more active conversation right now.Diggs' free agency stalled for months partly because teams were waiting on the outcome of an NFL personal conduct investigation tied to an alleged incident involving his former chef. That cleared up in June when the league announced there was insufficient evidence to support a violation, removing a major hurdle for suitors who'd been sitting on the sidelines.Fowler also notes a key difference from last year: Diggs enters this market fully healthy, not rehabbing the torn ACL that limited him during his lone Patriots season. Despite that, he still played roughly 55% of New England's offensive snaps and cleared 1,000 yards, a track record that's kept his market alive even at 32.Diggs is coming off a one-year "prove it" deal with the Patriots that was structured to let both sides evaluate fit. New England released him in March, citing his cap number and the pending legal matter, both of which have since resolved in his favor as he heads into a fresh market. No specific asking price has been reported yet, but as an outright free agent (not a trade candidate), any signing would come with no compensation owed to New England.Terry McLaurin would remain Washington's clear WR1, continuing to draw top coverage weekly. Still, Diggs' presence would give young quarterback Jayden Daniels a proven, savvy second option to attack softer looks underneath and in the slot. For a Commanders team that reached the divisional round with Super Bowl aspirations before slipping to a top-10 pick, adding a veteran of Diggs' caliber even at this stage of his career gives their receiver room real juice heading into the season.Nothing is finalized, and no contract has been reported yet. But with camps open, Diggs healthy, and his legal situation behind him, a decision looks close, and right now, all signs point to Washington.As training camp gets going, Stefon Diggs is still waiting for the right opportunity. The Commanders may be a strong possibility, but no deal has been made yet. For now, the veteran wide receiver is taking his time, and his next move is expected to be one of the biggest stories to watch before the regular season begins.
Article Summary: Stefon diggs remains a free agent with training camps already underway. The washington commanders are the clear favorite, according to espn's jeremy fowler. The baltimore ravens have also been mentioned as a fallback suitor. As an outright free agent, any signing would come with no compensation owed to new england.

Article Title: 'Why different rules for different players?' - Abhishek Sharma's poor form sparks Sanju Samson debate
Article Text:
India's Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson (ANI Photo)

Hanuma Vihari has questioned Team India's decision to continue backing Abhishek Sharma despite his poor run of form in the ongoing T20I series against Zimbabwe. The former India batter believes the selectors have applied different standards to Abhishek and Sanju Samson, especially after Samson lost his place despite performing well in major tournaments.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Vihari pointed out that Samson was dropped after a few poor games before the T20 World Cup but returned strongly to become one of India's standout performers.He said, "Before the World Cup, Sanju Samson did not perform in five games and lost his spot in the starting 11. He then made a comeback and became Player of the Tournament. In that same tournament, how many runs did Abhishek Sharma make?"He also highlighted Abhishek's recent numbers, saying, "In the UK series, apart from one fifty, there were no scores at all. Not even 20s and 30s, no significant score. One fifty in the last eight matches. If you include the World Cup, three half-centuries in the last 18 matches."Vihari argued that Samson proved himself when it mattered by scoring three consecutive fifties during India's T20 World Cup-winning campaign, but still lost his place in the side as youngster Vaibhav Sooryavanshi emerged as a preferred option.Questioning the selection policy, he said, "How many matches Samson played in the World Cup? Three. And fifties in all three. Abhishek's highest score in the five matches is 16. Why is no one talking about it? When it comes to Samson, they say he is inconsistent. Fair enough. But he can win high-pressure matches on his day."Vihari concluded by adding, "Abhishek is a player with a lot of hype, but Samson is also equal. He has also performed in the IPL. Why different rules for different players?"
Article Summary: Hanuma vihari has questioned team india's decision to continue backing abhishek sharma. The former india batter believes the selectors have applied different standards to sanju samson, especially after samson lost his place despite performing well in major tournaments. Samson was dropped after a few poor games before the t20 world cup.

Article Title: What the latest Baker Mayfield report really says about Tampa Bay's confidence in its $47 million franchise quarterback
Article Text:
Baker Mayfield (Getty Images)

Could the Buccaneers use the franchise tag instead of giving Baker Mayfield a new contract?

Baker Mayfield's contract situation in Tampa Bay is getting messier and more fascinating by the week. The Buccaneers quarterback is in the final year of a reworked deal worth $27 million in 2026, with no long-term extension anywhere close to the horizon. And now, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the franchise tag is emerging as a very real possibility for 2027 -- one that could cost Tampa Bay at least $47 million.A franchise tag has rarely been part of the public discussion around Mayfield's future, but Fowler believes it remains a realistic possibility."While Mayfield would prefer a long-term deal, he’s not afraid of the franchise tag, which would cost Tampa Bay at least $47M in 2027," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler wrote on his official X account on Sunday.From Mayfield's perspective, the financial risk appears limited. He has already earned significant money during his NFL career and is due another $40 million this season. That gives him room to be patient rather than force negotiations."Baker has made $131.8 million already in his career & he’ll make $40 million this season," Damage Inc. wrote on X on Sunday. "Getting tagged at $47 million at age 32 won’t faze him at all.I’m sure he would like another nine-digit contract, but he’s going to make over $200 million in his career regardless."While the financial side remains stable, Mayfield enters the season with something else to prove. Last year started in impressive fashion as both he and the Buccaneers looked like one of the NFL's biggest success stories through the first six weeks. That momentum faded quickly. Tampa Bay finished 8-9, missed the playoffs for the first time since 2019 and Mayfield's standing across the league took a hit.ESPN's annual survey of NFL executives, coaches and scouts reflected that shift. After previously being viewed among the league's top quarterbacks, Mayfield dropped out of the Top 10 and landed in the honourable mention category. He also missed out on the Pro Bowl after earning selections in each of his first two seasons with Tampa Bay.Even so, respect for his game has not disappeared. Mayfield was the only quarterback from the NFC South to receive votes in the rankings."Mayfield is a winner," one anonymous NFL coordinator told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. "He can make every throw. Fearless. Teammates seem to love to play for him."Mayfield himself has made it clear that contract talks are not his immediate focus, even if discussions have not progressed as hoped."(Contract extension talks) not anywhere close to what we were thinking," Mayfield told Tampa Bay Times NFL reporter Rick Stroud. "Would love to be here long term, but as of right now that’s not exactly the case. But I’m under contract for 2026. The guys in that locker room, the staff know that I’m still gonna be me. I’m still going to do everything I can to help this team win a Super Bowl. To me, that’s the priority. Everything else will take care of itself. "For now, the Buccaneers do not appear under pressure to make an immediate decision. A strong 2026 season could strengthen Mayfield's case for another long-term deal. If not, the franchise tag offers Tampa Bay another option while keeping its starting quarterback in place.
Article Summary: Baker mayfield is in the final year of a reworked deal worth $27 million in 2026. The franchise tag is emerging as a very real possibility for 2027. Tampa bay finished 8-9, missed the playoffs for the first time since 2019.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind” - How Rafael Nadal’s fam
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible. They give me peace of mind” - How Rafael Nadal’s family stood by him through every injury on his road to tennis immortality (Image via Getty)

How did Rafael Nadal overcome a career-threatening foot condition?

Why did Rafael Nadal always choose family and home over fame?

What did Rafael Nadal say about his wife and family during his injury battles?

What life lesson did Rafael Nadal learn from pain and defeat?

For years, Rafael Nadal inspired fans with his fight on the tennis court. What many people did not see was the battle he fought away from the spotlight. Long before becoming a 22-time Grand Slam champion, Nadal was told that a rare foot condition could end his career. He dealt with constant pain, serious injuries and doubts about whether he could keep playing. Yet he kept coming back. While his determination made headlines, Nadal has always said his biggest strength was the people who stood beside him. Their support helped him survive the hardest moments and build one of the greatest careers in tennis history.In 2005, Nadal won his first French Open title at just 19 years old. Soon after that breakthrough, he was diagnosed with Mueller-Weiss syndrome, a rare condition that affects the bones in the foot.Doctors warned that continuing his career at the highest level might not be possible.Instead of giving up, Nadal returned home to Manacor in Mallorca. There, he was surrounded by his father Sebastián, mother Ana María, sister Maribel and his longtime partner Mery Perelló. Their support gave him the strength to keep moving forward when his future looked uncertain.Looking back on those difficult years, Nadal once said:“Without the people that I have around me, all these years, without my family, without my team, it would be impossible.They give me peace of mind.”Despite becoming one of the biggest names in world sport, Nadal never left the place where he grew up. He stayed close to his family in Manacor and continued living the simple life that had shaped him from childhood.His uncle and longtime coach Toni Nadal taught him to stay humble, respect opponents and never believe he was bigger than the game. Those lessons stayed with him throughout his career.Nadal has often explained that returning home helped him switch off from the pressure of professional tennis. In Manacor, he was simply Rafa, spending time with friends and family. That normal life became an important part of maintaining his mental balance through the highs and lows of the sport.Nadal’s wife, Mery “Xisca” Perelló, was by his side long before he became a global star. She witnessed every comeback, every rehabilitation session and every painful setback that fans rarely saw.As injuries continued in the final years of his career, those shared sacrifices became even more meaningful. With his wife, young son and team watching from the stands, Nadal reflected on everything they had gone through together.He said:“Having my family here, my wife, my son, my team… it’s emotional because they know how hard the process has been. They have been through the good moments, but especially the tough moments during all these years of injuries.”Nadal never believed success came without suffering. Throughout his career, he played through injuries, long matches and physical pain that would have stopped many athletes. Instead of running from those challenges, he accepted them as part of the journey.That mindset became one of the biggest reasons behind his remarkable career.As Nadal explained:“If you don’t lose, you cannot enjoy the victories. You have to accept both things. I learned during my career to enjoy suffering.”His story goes far beyond Grand Slam trophies or records. It shows that true strength is not only about winning titles but also about staying grounded when life becomes difficult. Through every injury and every comeback, Nadal never lost sight of the people who mattered most. Their love gave him the peace, confidence and support to keep chasing his dreams, making his journey one of the most inspiring stories in modern sport.
Article Summary: Rafael nadal was diagnosed with a career-threatening foot condition in 2005. The spaniard returned home to manacor in mallorca to be with his family. Nadal has always said his biggest strength was the people who stood beside him. His uncle and longtime coach toni nadal taught him to stay humble.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal challengers bengaluru (rcb) beat chennai super kings (csk) in ipl 2026 encounter at the m chinnaswamy stadium on sunday. Rcb register their second win over csk in the ipl. Tim david, rajat patidar and devdutt padikkal all scored half-centuries for rcb. Bhuvneshwar kumar took 3-41 to help rcb reach 250/3.
